title: JAH Scaling Law Fitter
summary: Signature-authored method: fit your own scaling curves from small runs before committing.
details: JAH Scaling Law Fitter is a JAH-designed procedure: run a ladder of small models (10M to 1B), fit loss-vs-compute power laws, and extrapolate to pick the compute-optimal size for your budget — your own Chinchilla, calibrated to your data. Includes confidence bands so extrapolation risk is explicit. Labeled Signature; an original JAH procedure.

demo.title: Power-law fit sketch
demo.program:
import math
runs = [(1e18, 3.2), (1e19, 2.9), (1e20, 2.65)]  # (flops, loss)
xs = [math.log10(f) for f, _ in runs]; ys = [l for _, l in runs]
n = len(runs)
slope = (n*sum(a*b for a, b in zip(xs, ys)) - sum(xs)*sum(ys)) /         (n*sum(a*a for a in xs) - sum(xs)**2)
print("loss slope per decade:", round(slope, 3))
